entries.reason: After the acting tenant is resolved each of these mutations now calls requireTenantProduct(tenantContext.tenantId, "academy"), refusing 403 product_not_entitled when the tenant was not provisioned with the product and 503 entitlement_unavailable when the entitlement cannot be read (multi-tenant #20, section 3.3 of MULTI_TENANT_WHITE_LABEL_ARCHITECTURE.md). platform_tenants.products[] existed since migration 0001, was carried on the Tenant type, and was read by nothing: a tenant provisioned without Academy was served every Academy route exactly like one that bought it, and route-guards.ts (requireTenant / requireFeature) had no importer anywhere in src. The gate ANDs the platform feature flag with the tenant entitlement and is fail-closed on both — an absent tenant, an empty products[] and an unreadable entitlement are all refused. Each of these operations changes only its sourceHash from the added guard; no classification, principalSource, tenantSource or existing control changed, verified by comparison against the effective manifest, which is why every entry is re-pinned rather than rewritten. The gate is placed immediately after the tenantContext.available check so it reads the tenant the request acts in, never the platform default; a source guard in tenant-scoped-route-guards.test.ts pins one gate per resolved tenant on each route, and tenant-product-entitlement-postgres.test.ts proves the refusals against a provisioned database.
